newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA- NEW CAR SALES RISE IN H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA- NEW CAR SALES RISE IN H1 1997.

text.p: New car sales in Lithuania, Ladas excluded, rose to 1,836 in the first half of 1997 from 1,263 in the same period last year, Auto Research, a local marketing research company, said on Wednesday.
Robertas Cickevichius, the head of the firm's research division, said that 1,370 of the cars were acquired by Lithuanian clients and 466 cars were bought by foreign citizens.
He also said that 434 cars were bought by individuals and 1,402 cars were sold to companies and institutions.
Of the total, 1,449 were passenger cars, of which 387 were compacts.
Volkswagen had a 38 percent share of the market with 699 new cars sold, followed by General Motors with 229 cars sold and a 12 percent market share.
Ford Motors sold 161 new cars in the first half of 1997 and had nine percent of the market.
Skoda Felicia was the most popular model in the passenger car group and 285 cars were sold.
It was followed by VW Passat (88 cars sold), VW Golf/Vento (74 cars sold), Opel Vectra (60 cars sold), Opel Astra (59 cars sold), Mazda 626 (57 cars sold) and Honda Civic (52 cars sold).
Cickevichius said that the increase in new car sales stemmed from the improving economic situation in the country, the low exchange rate of the German mark and the growth in leasing services.
He added that if present tendencies remain new car sales will reach 3,500 in 1997, a 30 percent rise from 1996.
Cickevichius also said that 1,298 Ladas were sold in the first half of 1997. Only 46 of them remained in Lithuania while the rest were exported to CIS countries.
